title: Title and standfirst after body HITL, not in the first scan
description:
# Headline pass: body, then title, then subtitle

## Intent

As a copy-editing agent, I want to finish the article body first, then name it, then write the subtitle, so the title and subtitle flow together and the subtitle can summarize the piece we actually have.

## Why this order

Body edits can change what the piece is. The subtitle is a **short summary of the entire article**, so it cannot be written until the working-copy body is settled. The title comes **before** the subtitle so the summary can see the chosen title and sit under it instead of competing with an old headline or being written in the dark.

Order:

1. Article (body HITL on a working copy)
2. Title (sees the working-copy body)
3. Subtitle (sees the working-copy body **and** the title just applied)

Never: title/subtitle in the first body `scan`. Never subtitle before title.

## Schema is publication-owned

Frontmatter keys are not portable. Anth.us uses `title` + `excerpt`. Pilobolus and Chattic.us use `title` + `standfirst`. Some drafts have no YAML. Limatus must not hardcode `standfirst`.

The engine knows two **jobs**, not a CMS schema:

- `title` — names the piece
- `subtitle` — short summary of the whole article

The style profile **binds** those jobs to keys and says when the passes run.

```yaml
headline:
  when: afterBody          # afterBody (our default in house profiles) | never
  order: [title, subtitle]
  title:
    key: title
  subtitle:
    key: standfirst       # or excerpt, dek, subtitle — whatever this pub stores
    role: articleSummary
```

- If `headline` is omitted, Limatus does **not** guess keys. No headline pass. Portable callers stay schema-agnostic.
- House profiles (Pilobolus, Anth.us, Chattic.us) **do** ship this block with `when: afterBody` and `order: [title, subtitle]`.
- `description` / OG / SEO fields are not the subtitle unless the profile points `subtitle.key` at them.

Existing `standfirst:` shape checks (length, insider terms) remain optional constraints on the subtitle **job** once the key is bound. They are not a second schema.

## Context each pass sees

- **Title options:** working-copy body only (plus voice/aim). Not the old subtitle as gospel; that field may still describe a previous draft.
- **Subtitle options:** working-copy body **and** the title now on that working copy. The model must be able to read both so the dek follows the headline.
- Apply writes only the bound YAML value on the working copy. `--original` is never written.

## Done when

- Body `limatus scan` does not emit title/subtitle findings.
- Title pass can run only against a working copy; options receive the current body.
- Subtitle pass refuses to run unless a title is present on that working copy; options receive body + that title.
- Binding comes from the profile (`headline.title.key`, `headline.subtitle.key`), not from hardcoded `standfirst`.
- House profiles default `when: afterBody`, `order: [title, subtitle]`.
- Apply of a title option does not rewrite the subtitle, and vice versa.

## Out of scope

Auto-picking the title. Mixing title and subtitle into one rewrite. Guessing frontmatter keys when `headline` is absent.

```gherkin
Feature: Title then subtitle after the article
  As a copy-editing agent
  I want body HITL, then title, then subtitle
  So the subtitle can summarize this article under this title

  Scenario: Body scan does not flag title or subtitle fields
    Given a working copy with YAML title and subtitle keys from the profile
    When I run limatus scan
    Then the diagnosis has no title or subtitle findings

  Scenario: Title pass sees the working-copy body
    Given a working copy whose body HITL is finished
    When I generate title options
    Then each option rewrites only the configured title key
    And the option prompt includes the working-copy body

  Scenario: Subtitle pass sees title and body
    Given a working copy with a newly applied title
    When I generate subtitle options
    Then each option rewrites only the configured subtitle key
    And the option prompt includes that title and the working-copy body
    And the original file is unchanged
```
